passage_text: Researchers studied the impact of sleep deprivation on short‑term memory recall. Twenty‑eight healthy adults were randomly assigned to one of three groups: (1) Control (normal sleep, 8 h/night), (2) 4‑hour sleep (restricted to 4 h/night for 3 days), and (3) 6‑hour sleep (restricted to 6 h/night for 3 days). After the sleep period, participants completed a standardized word‑list recall test. The mean recall scores and standard deviations were recorded. The study aimed to determine whether reduced sleep duration impairs memory performance and whether partial sleep restriction (6 h) mitigates the effect compared to severe restriction (4 h).
stem: Which group had the highest mean recall score?
explanation: Correct: Control mean was 85, above 78 (6-hour) and 68 (4-hour). Why the others are wrong: B) 4-hour mean (68) was the lowest. C) 6-hour mean (78) was below the Control mean of 85. D) The three means (85, 78, 68) differ.
trap: Assuming a group with some restriction still performs best because it slept more than the 4-hour group.

stem: Which of the following is a potential confounding variable in this study?

options.C: Use of a standardized recall test

explanation: Caffeine intake can affect alertness and memory performance, making it a potential confounder. Random assignment, standardized testing, and controlled sleep duration help reduce confounding.
trap: Assuming random assignment itself is a confounder.

stem: What is the difference in mean recall between the Control and 4‑hour sleep groups?
explanation: Control mean = 85, 4‑hour sleep mean = 68. Difference = 85 – 68 = 17 points.
trap: Subtracting the 4-hour mean from the 6-hour mean (78 − 68 = 10) instead of from the Control mean (85 − 68 = 17).

stem: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.A: The Control group had the highest mean recall score.
options.B: The 4-hour sleep group had the lowest mean recall score.
options.C: The 6-hour sleep group performed better than the 4-hour sleep group.
options.D: The 6-hour sleep group had a larger sample size than the Control group.

explanation: Correct: the 6-hour group had 8 participants versus 10 in Control, so it was smaller. Why the others are wrong: A) 85 is the highest mean. B) 68 is the lowest mean. C) 78 > 68.
trap: Assuming all three groups had equal n, or reading the 6-hour group's n of 8 as larger than Control's 10, so statement D seems correct.

stem: Which comparison between two groups shows the smallest difference in mean recall score?
explanation: Correct: 85 - 78 = 7 points, smaller than 10 and 17. Why the others are wrong: A) 85 - 68 = 17, the largest difference. C) 78 - 68 = 10, larger than 7. D) The differences are 17, 7 and 10.
trap: Assuming the two sleep-restricted groups must be the most similar (6-hour vs 4-hour, 10 points apart), when Control and 6-hour differ by only 7 points.
